demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Smart and connected lighting is one of the fastest-growing segments, expanding at over approx. 20% annually in certain sub-segments, driven by IoT-enabled luminaires, motion sensors, daylight harvesting systems and building-management-system integration.
- Outdoor and street lighting is poised for substantial expansion, supported by the Smart Cities Mission, municipal energy-efficiency mandates and retrofitting programmes replacing legacy systems.
- Urban infrastructure spending, smart city initiatives and energy-efficiency regulations continue to favour LED and connected lighting solutions, underpinning overall industry growth momentum.
- Revenue from operations grew due to higher sales volumes, market/product expansion, effective pricing strategies and improved customer acquisition and retention, though profit after tax declined as higher operating, employee, input, finance and depreciation costs outpaced revenue growth.
- Company secured infrastructure orders from Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation and Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation for architectural and city-beautification lighting, including a three-year O&M contract, strengthening its order book in the infrastructure segment.
- Company secured commercial orders from clients including Larsen & Toubro Limited (Construction), Avid AV Technologies, PSP Projects, Disha Retail Fixtures and Lightalive Solutions.
- Company secured residential orders from Suryam Developers LLP and Marwadi Educare Foundation.
- Wholly-owned subsidiary Plus Light Tech F.Z.E secured a retail project order from Centrepoint (Landmark Retail Investment Co. L.L.C.) in the UAE.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Domestic and international players drive commoditization in LED products, creating downward pricing pressure, particularly in budget segments; unorganized-sector low-cost alternatives exacerbate margin challenges.
- Institutional, infrastructure and government projects are susceptible to delays, cancellations or funding constraints; seasonal demand fluctuations and uneven rural electrification add unpredictability.
- Penetration in semi-urban and rural markets is constrained by affordability issues, limited retail infrastructure and low awareness of energy-efficient lighting benefits.
- Rapid changes in design trends, smart-lighting expectations and sustainability demands can make certain product lines less relevant if not updated regularly.
- Dependence on imported LEDs, drivers and control modules exposes the Company to disruptions from geopolitical tensions, port delays and currency fluctuations.
- An extensive market for counterfeit and substandard lighting products, thriving on complex distribution channels, hurts brand trust, margins and compliant players.
- Innovations such as Li-Fi, smart controls, IoT integration and adaptive human-centric lighting require continuous R&D investment; failure to keep pace could render existing products less competitive.
- Inadequate transport networks, warehousing limitations and inconsistent power supply can impact distribution efficiency and project timelines; rising demand for engineers, technicians and IoT specialists may outpace the talent pipeline.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Focus on innovation, operational efficiency, customer-centricity, and sustainable lighting solutions to continually expand footprint in domestic and international markets.
- Continue improving operational efficiencies and optimizing cost structure to strengthen margins.
